answer.text:
Acme signed off UAT for core replenishment only, not for the programme as a whole. Lena Fischer, Acme's Head of Supply Chain, signed the sign-off on 22 January 2025. [1]

The signed wording was: "Acme Org confirms that user acceptance testing for core replenishment has been completed satisfactorily for the 25 store pilot cohort, covering ambient and dry goods categories. This sign-off does not extend to fresh categories, which remain in scope for a later phase, and does not constitute acceptance of the overall programme." The scope was deliberately narrow: the 25-store pilot cohort, ambient and dry goods only, with fresh explicitly excluded and no acceptance of the overall programme. [2]

At the UAT readiness review on 21 January 2025, Lena Fischer said: "I want to be careful. I am signing that ambient core replenishment works for twenty-five stores, not that the project is finished." [3] [4] [5]

Two UAT defects were open at the time the sign-off wording was circulated, both the same root cause on case pack and minimum order quantity rounding, and neither was a blocker. Kwame Boateng later confirmed both rounding defects were fixed and re-tested, with nine of nine scenarios passing. [2] [6]

No evidence in the archive shows any UAT sign-off covering fresh categories. Fresh UAT ran later in 2025, and a go/no-go decision in November 2025 approved produce, dairy and chilled while bakery was descoped; fresh go-live followed on 15 December 2025. No separate fresh UAT sign-off is recorded. [7] [8] [9]
